text:
Brayden Schenn, 35, a Stanley Cup winner in St. Louis, has become one of the Islanders' quiet stories. He had three points in the Nov. 12 win over the Kings that ended a four-game winless run, and the New York Post wrote about him mentoring rookie Victor Eklund. He has 15 points in 20 games, already a healthy pace next to last season's 39 in 80.

Our numbers aren't buying all of it. The Islanders have been outchanced with him on at five on five (46% of the expected goals, five points worse than without him), and they've scored seven more goals than those chances deserve when he's out there. He's also shooting 18%, against the 14% we'd expect. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season.

What he still does well is move the puck: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 68% of his exits leaving the zone with possession. On a team riding goaltending and hot finishing to a three-game win streak, Schenn is a useful veteran whose points are running ahead of his play.
